A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BrepARG work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. V1 ends with references; v2 supplies Appendix A. Inspection of all pages supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation results, efficiency measurements, sampling and ordering ablations, and qualitative generated examples in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds BrepDiff comparisons and quantitative tokenization ablations in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The token representation, shared face-edge VQ-VAE, scalar position quantization, DFS/MAX-IDX-A ordering, autoregressive model and detokenization procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A provides additional loss and matching details, without establishing a revision to the previously described method.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepCAD and ABC for unconditional generation and Furniture for class-conditioned generation. The appendix examines existing geometry and position tokenization components without introducing another dataset, application domain or generation task.

E2.justification: V2 adds BrepDiff to the DeepCAD generation comparison in Table 1 and the efficiency comparison in Table 2. Existing benchmark comparators remain. Newly discussed AutoBrep and BrepGPT are not included in the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The added ablations introduce reconstruction evaluation using a shared subset of 3,000 DeepCAD test B-reps, controlled codebook-size variation, and bounding-box accuracy at an absolute tolerance of 0.01. The existing generation sample counts, metrics and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2 and A.3 add substantial component analyses: codebook size versus reconstruction fidelity and validity, and four learned bounding-box quantization schemes versus the scalar-quantization rationale. V1 supplies qualitative position-tokenization observations but lacks these quantitative studies. Existing sampling and ordering ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over 10 independent runs for Table 1. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance procedures for the new appendix results.

E6.justification: Previously reported scores remain unchanged, while v2 adds substantial result entries. BrepDiff obtains 62.83% validity, with 1.8-day training and 8.3-second inference. Table 6 reports reconstruction validity from 69.8% at codebook size 512 to 87.5% at 4,096; Table 7 reports learned position-quantizer accuracies of 96.4–99.4%. These are added comparisons and component results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly defines face and edge ordering objectives, relates them to constrained minimum linear arrangement, and derives edge-order invariance and conflicting face-order preferences. Appendix A.3 also derives a scalar-quantization error bound. These substantially extend v1's mathematical treatment, although Equation 14 omits the two-face multiplicity present in Equation 13.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a first holistic geometry-topology token sequence, autoregressive B-rep generation, state-of-the-art performance and improved efficiency. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A substantially expands the rationale concerning codebook capacity, utilization and vocabulary cost, scalar-quantization reliability, and competing ordering objectives. It explains MAX-IDX-A through the distribution of positional offsets despite invariant total edge-face distance, extending v1's simpler locality explanation. The existing quantization-loss and long-sequence limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code access link and substantially expands technical documentation: cosine-similarity codebook matching, VQ-VAE loss and update details, quantization-ablation architectures, spectral-ordering implementation and random tie-breaking for MAX-IDX-A. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 substantially revises the closest-work positioning: v1 emphasizes SolidGen and largely unexplored direct serialization, whereas v2 acknowledges concurrent AutoBrep and BrepGPT and explains differences from AutoBrep. BrepDiff is newly cited, and the characterization of Hola is revised.

P1.justification: V2 adds Appendix A and acknowledgements, rewrites portions of related work, and clarifies the ordering-ablation description. The main section organization and most existing prose remain intact; the added scientific content does not constitute extensive rewriting of the original narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–7, expands Tables 1–2 with BrepDiff rows, and refreshes the rendering and arrangement of diagrams including Figures 1, 2 and 4. The overall layout, qualitative examples and existing table organization remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 provide quantitative support for tokenization choices that v1 largely motivated qualitatively. The additional baseline, closer related-work positioning and implementation disclosures also strengthen the paper while leaving its main empirical findings unchanged. These benefits outweigh a localized defect in the new ordering analysis: Equation 14 drops the two-face multiplicity from Equation 13, although the edge-order invariance conclusion survives.
